failures.evidence: Red test TestTwoPodsReceiveConnectionLostToADroppingRouteReleasesTheLeaseWithin15s (packages/envoy/cmd/listener/multiprocess_takeover_test.go, with mpLaneRelay.blackholeNew in multiprocess_harness_test.go, commit 'test(envoy-listener): red row for a receive connection lost to a route that drops its packets'). Command: cd packages/envoy && go test -tags multiprocess -count=3 -timeout 20m -run '^TestTwoPodsReceiveConnectionLostToADroppingRouteReleasesTheLeaseWithin15s$' -v ./cmd/listener -> FAIL 3 of 3 at ff705a78 (twice '10 of 150 messages reached their session later than 15s', first at 15.966s; once 'pod-a never released the lease for its lost receive connection'). Real-binary run (cut.py recv, 7 runs): the standby takes the EXPIRED lease at 7.94 s in 5 runs, with first delivery 13.95 s after the cut; in 2 runs the lease is released only at 9.85 s, with first delivery at 15.95 s. Cause, from a SIGQUIT goroutine dump of pod-a 5.5 s into the cut: lease.step -> receiveDown -> durableReceiver.receiveUp -> bus.Client.Connected -> nats.Conn.Status blocks on the connection RWMutex, which nats.go doReconnect -> processConnectInit holds while it waits for the INFO of a reconnect that never answers. So the lease loop, renewals included, stalls whenever the receive connection's reconnect dials hang (a route that drops packets, a blackholed hub address).
